investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements, leaving only those 2 eligible nodes — both of which report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm." Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on either eligible node. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window remained unschedulable for ~143–147 seconds before the checks timed out, and no VM identity or state was ever returned to the eval runner. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary (high confidence): The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes. All 3 concurrent or sequential remote-agent eval pods were rejected with 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', and preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are holding the resource that could be evicted.

Secondary (medium confidence): A prior eval run or external workload created remote-agent VMs that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new pods from scheduling. The eval runner uses withCleanup() (run-status-probes.mjs:1883), but if a previous run crashed before cleanup, leaked VMs could be occupying capacity.

Tertiary (lower confidence): The node affinity or selector on the remote-agent pod spec is misconfigured or has drifted such that only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible, reducing the effective scheduling pool to the 2 already-saturated kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes. This would compound any capacity pressure.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and unallocated on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission cause would need to be investigated.

If re-running the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike in VM usage) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the node affinity/selector is corrected to include them, and the eval then passes, the root cause would be a misconfigured node selector rather than absolute capacity exhaustion.
If leaked pods from prior eval runs are found and deleted, and the eval subsequently passes, the root cause would be cleanup failure rather than insufficient total cluster capacity.

Add a leaked-resource detection eval that lists all remote-agent pods older than the eval cleanup window and fails if any are found, catching withCleanup() failures before they exhaust VM capacity.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the remote-agent pod's nodeAffinity and nodeSelector match at least a minimum number of healthy nodes, catching selector drift before it reduces the eligible scheduling pool.

Consider adding a separate eval for the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool health (node count, resource availability) as a prerequisite check that gates the remote-agent-create eval, making the dependency chain explicit in the feature registry.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-21T20:45–20:50Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the production cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the eval's remote-agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource report insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler rejected the remote-agent pod on all 6 production nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" (resource quota exhausted or limit reached), and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~143–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent) could not create a remote agent, and the check returned no evidence, violating the remote-agent-state contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This is the most directly supported cause given the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message appearing identically across all three sibling checks.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only the 2 kata-capable nodes carry, and those 2 nodes are already at capacity. This is a structural constraint, not a transient error.

Concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all VM slots: if other eval runs, user workloads, or leaked pods from prior eval cleanup are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations, new pods cannot be scheduled until those are released.

Cluster under-provisioned for the current remote-agent load: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, and the total VM capacity across those nodes is insufficient to absorb simultaneous eval probe runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was stuck unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements, leaving only those 2 eligible nodes — both of which report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm." Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were found on either eligible node. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window remained unschedulable for ~143–147 seconds before the checks timed out, and no VM identity or state was ever returned to the eval runner. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

All 3 concurrent or sequential remote-agent eval pods were rejected with 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', and preemption found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are holding the resource that could be evicted.

Secondary (medium confidence): A prior eval run or external workload created remote-agent VMs that were not cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new pods from scheduling. investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-21T20:45–20:50Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the production cluster's 6 nodes cannot schedule the eval's remote-agent pod because the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource report insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and consequently no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler rejected the remote-agent pod on all 6 production nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" (resource quota exhausted or limit reached), and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~143–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent) could not create a remote agent, and the check returned no evidence, violating the remote-agent-state contract (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the remote-agent-state eval that produces a schedulable pod and returns all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) would indicate the capacity issue was transient and has self-resolved.

kubectl node inspection showing that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and no pods are consuming it would disprove the resource-exhaustion hypothesis and point to a different scheduling constraint.
Evidence that the remote-agent pod spec's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes would shift the root cause from capacity exhaustion to a misconfiguration.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime (sibling checks) while remote-agent-state continues to fail would suggest the failure is isolated to the state-polling path rather than a shared VM capacity problem.

Cluster event logs showing the 2 kata-capable nodes were cordoned, drained, or had their VM resource limit reduced around 2026-07-21T20:45Z would confirm a deliberate infrastructure change rather than organic capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the cluster before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'warn' signal rather than a timeout failure.
Add a 'remote-agent-cleanup' eval that verifies no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each eval run, catching withCleanup failures that could leak VM slot allocations.

Add a sibling check for node affinity/selector health that verifies the expected number of kata-capable nodes are schedulable and not cordoned, providing early warning before VM capacity is exhausted.

Introduce a historical baseline eval that tracks the pass/fail trend for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime across runs, enabling regression detection when the feature transitions from passing to failing for the first time.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable — Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-21T20:45–20:50Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could accept the pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, no agent was created, no runtime response was produced, and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are entirely absent from the eval result.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the two eligible nodes. The remaining four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod request timed out unscheduled (~143–147 s each), preventing agent creation and making all downstream eval assertions unreachable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents swarm scheduling path, not a code defect or eval infrastructure failure.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent(..., 'remote', ...) — the pod scheduling failure blocks createAgent before any evidence can be gathered
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes — no capacity remained for new peer-pod VMs at the time of the eval run, causing all three checks to fail with the same scheduler rejection

Secondary: node affinity/selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec restrict scheduling to only 2 of 6 nodes, making the cluster effectively a 2-node pool for remote agents and amplifying any capacity pressure

Tertiary: a concurrent workload or a prior eval run's pods not yet fully terminated may have consumed the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the eligible nodes, leaving zero capacity for the eval pods

Lower probability: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource extended by the node plugin was not re-advertised after a node restart or plugin failure, causing the resource count to appear at zero even if physical capacity exists

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages explicitly names Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on 2 nodes as the blocking condition for all three remote-agent pod requests.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to 2 nodes and concentrating all kata.peerpods.io/vm pressure there.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents eval feature — all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks registered under the remote-agents feature (features.json lines 183–185) failed in the same eval run window, indicating the shared pod scheduling dependency is the single point of failure.

affectedAreas.label: Eval runner — createAgent remote path
affectedAreas.reason: The runner at line 1918 calls createAgent(..., 'remote', ...) which triggers the pod scheduling request that the cluster cannot fulfill; no evidence is collected before this call returns an error.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to confirm whether capacity is exhausted or the resource is mis-advertised.
Audit all currently running or stuck remote-agent pods for leaked resources; terminate any pods in Terminating or long-running Pending state that may be holding vm slots.
If capacity is genuinely exhausted, scale up kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on existing eligible nodes or add additional nodes that satisfy the pod affinity/selector rules.
Review the pod node affinity/selector configuration to determine whether the restriction to 2 of 6 nodes is intentional; if not, expanding the eligible node pool would reduce scheduling pressure.
Set up a Kubernetes event or alert on Unschedulable pod events for the remote-agents namespace so capacity exhaustion is detected before the next eval run.

After cluster remediation, re-run all three remote-agents eval checks and confirm all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are present and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

Note: this is an eval-detected infrastructure failure. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; do not treat this as a confirmed user-facing outage until traffic signals are obtained.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agents sibling checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared scheduling dependency causes all three to fail together, validating the single-point-of-failure hypothesis.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the two affinity-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable > 0 and used = 0 at the time of the eval run, the capacity exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a plugin or API-level failure would need to be investigated instead.

If the eval passes cleanly on an immediate re-run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike (e.g., a concurrent workload that has since terminated) rather than a sustained quota exhaustion.
If only remote-agent-runtime failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state passed, the failure would be localized to the runtime probe path rather than the shared pod scheduling layer.

If the node affinity/selector rules were recently changed to restrict to fewer nodes, that change would be a contributing cause; absence of such a change in the cluster config would keep the focus on capacity.
If a kata-containers or peer-pods node plugin restart or misconfiguration is found on the eligible nodes, that would point to a resource advertisement failure rather than true capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested on affinity-eligible nodes and warns before capacity reaches zero, providing earlier signal than waiting for a pod to time out unscheduled.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that fires a warning if a remote-agent pod takes longer than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s) to reach Running state, catching capacity pressure before it causes full scheduling failures.
Add an eval that counts currently Pending or Terminating remote-agent pods and alerts if the count exceeds a threshold, detecting leaked pods that consume vm slots.

Consider a synthetic eval that verifies the node affinity/selector rules match the expected set of eligible nodes, catching accidental affinity misconfigurations before they reduce the schedulable pool.
